pr_body:
**- What I did**

- fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/21199
- fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/35195
- fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/45402
- fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/48527
- replaces the workaround added in https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48322

The default IPAM allocator is unable to represent subnets larger than 64-bits (subnets with a smaller prefix), because it uses a Bitmap that's limited to 64-bits.

When it's used to represent a 64-bit subnet, the top address can't be allocated (because bitmap.Bitmap is initialised with the number of bits it needs to represent in a uint64, so it's one short).

The rest of the daemon doesn't know about these limitations, so strange things happen when a large IPv6 subnet is used. No errors are reported, addresses/subnets are just set up incorrectly.  The IPAM code calculates offsets into the bitmap itself, details it shouldn't need to understand and, because it's working on offsets into a range it doesn't always notice when it's asked to set a bit outside the range (see the notes about "offset" in https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48319).

It's unusual to need a big subnet but, for example, it may be useful for modelling an ISP network, or an ISP's gateway may be in a "/56" subnet that's outside a 64-bit range used by hosts.

**- How I did it**

- Don't increment "unselected" in Bitmap when clearing a 0
  - Bug fix in the bitmap.Bitmap code
- Add addrset.AddrSet to track a set of IP addresses
  - A new internal package to track IP addresses.
  - It owns a `bitmap.Bitmap` for each range of up to 63-bits that has a bit set, within the subnet it's asked to represent.
- Use addrset.AddrSet instead of bitmap.Bitmap in IPAM

**- How to verify it**

New unit tests for `AddrSet`, plus existing tests (including the two "XFAIL" tests that now pass).

**- Description for the changelog**
```markdown changelog
- IPAM now handles subnets bigger than "/64".
```
pr_comments: I've added an extra commit, just to clarify the code that reserves network/broadcast addresses.

issue_context.body:
### Description

It seems like any other then the last block in an ipv6 address is ignored when trying to assign static IPs.

### Reproduce

```
# create a network with v6 enabled
mava@server01:~/projects/schema-server$ docker network create --ipv6 --subnet fd1a:b128::/32 mynet123
ebba0bf437a9d8f9ff4f1e245c3b09e65cbaa7c58ad235efd7bdd14bb91b0e38
# create first container
mava@server01:~/projects/schema-server$ docker run --name u1 -d --net mynet123 --ip6 fd1a:b128:5901::101 ubuntu sleep 999
ca4d0eaf28ba46a61cd75a17ff73b4679d2c2f3624e739dc4fca7a190763c6a7
# create second container
mava@server01:~/projects/schema-server$ docker run --name u2 -d --net mynet123 --ip6 fd1a:b128:5902::101 ubuntu sleep 999
50dbecfb20b881cddd9488839d464c7a10d63f72cb5a2261824e8db8db2f863c
docker: Error response from daemon: Address already in use.
```

Due to limitations in how Docker Engine tracks IP address assignments, the interface ID of container interface addresses is truncated to 64 bits. I'd like to know more about your use-case; why do you need more than 2^64 interface addresses in a single bridge network?

```console
$ docker network create --ipv6 --subnet fd1a:b128::/32 myv6net

3973339bf0c61e93f28ecf3a514fb40e04da7a258051ab50c6e4d41db0e2c13d
$ docker exec v6wut ip a
```

Hi @corhere 
this is not about having >2^64 ifaces, but rather about being able to provide static ipv6 addresses for interfaces.

In [containerlab](https://containerlab.dev) we provide a cli tool to create network labs using docker runtime, and in networking it is often desirable to have statically assigned addresses for mgmt network.

Now that you mentioned that docker/moby strips user-provided ipv6 address by leftmost 64b it becomes clear why we saw address collision for two distinct IPv6 addresses pointed out in the origin of this issue.

It is a bit strange this is not noted in the docs for the `--ip6` flag...

> this is not about having >2^64 ifaces, but rather about being able to provide static ipv6 addresses for interfaces.

While the above is true, there is a use case for having all 2^128 addresses usable when simulating (network) designs.

Hi @corhere 

> I'd like to know more about your use-case; why do you need more than 2^64 interface addresses in a single bridge network?

I'm modeling a real network in Docker for software testing.  One of the services uses information encoded into the third segment of the IPv6 address.  Ideally, we'd have a /16 IPv6 network, giving us full control over the third segment for each instance of the service.

While it may be possible to patch the service to find the information in the last 64 bits, we'd no longer be testing a faithful model of the production environment.

review_comments:
Curious; can the new package fully replace (direct uses of) the  `bitmap` package? After this PR it's imported in 2 locations, so I was wondering if those would also switch over?

```bash
git grep '"github.com/docker/docker/libnetwork/bitmap"'
libnetwork/drivers/overlay/ovmanager/ovmanager.go:      "github.com/docker/docker/libnetwork/bitmap"
libnetwork/internal/addrset/addrset.go: "github.com/docker/docker/libnetwork/bitmap"
```

The overlay network's bitmap is tracking vlan ids (not IP addresses).

The other one is the new `AddrSet`, which is implemented using the bitmap.
Ah! Gotcha! Didn't go that deep comparing 👍

I guess I was wondering if we have some option to alias some of the types so that we don't have to introduce yet-another set of errors 😅, e.g.


```suggestion
	// ErrNotAvailable is returned when no more addresses are available to set
	ErrNotAvailable = ipamapi.ErrNoAvailableIPs
	// ErrAllocated is returned when the specific address requested is already allocated
	ErrAllocated = ipamapi.ErrIPAlreadyAllocated
```

or

```suggestion
	// ErrNotAvailable is returned when no more addresses are available to set
	ErrNotAvailable = bitmap.ErrBitAllocated
	// ErrAllocated is returned when the specific address requested is already allocated
	ErrAllocated = bitmap.ErrNoBitAvailable
```

(but the bitmap errors don't implement `errdefs` types)

The bitmap error texts talk about "bits" being available, but this new package is dealing with a set of addresses. So, bitmap's error messages didn't really make sense - and maybe we'll want to represent the address set differently at some point.

It didn't seem right for `AddrSet` to return IPAM errors, even though it's only used by `defaultipam` at the moment. But if you think it should, I can do that? (Could make package `addrset` internal to `defaultipam` so that it can't be used by anything else?)

Yeah, it was mostly wishful thinking on this one; libnetwork had a bit of a tendency to define errors for everything, even for those not actually checked for; in some cases that led to tighter coupling than needed.

So I was looking if it would be possible somehow to get closer to our errdefs definitions for matching specific conditions, but otherwise keep things generic.

This is all internal, so not a huge deal (doesn't expand public APIs / contracts.
